_documentation: Auditex CE+ practice run action catalogue. For each Cyber Essentials requirement it lists the proof actions a practice run can name, the conflicts it checks between policy and state rules, and the five CE+ assessor tests. Ranking weights are Auditex product defaults, not scheme rules. Contains public sector information from the NCSC Cyber Essentials: Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.3, licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0 (https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/sites/default/files/documents/cyber-essentials-requirements-for-it-infrastructure-v3-3.pdf). The wording is Auditex's own and copies no self-assessment question text.

source.document_title: Cyber Essentials: Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.3

requirement_notes.evidence_limits: Device and boundary firewalls sit outside the cloud tenant, so tenant data shows nothing here.
Firewall admin interfaces and their passwords are outside the cloud tenant.
Inbound firewall rules and their approval records are outside the cloud tenant.
The assessor checks internet exposure with a remote scan; tenant data is not an exposure scan.
For the cloud service the provider runs the firewall; the proof is your contract or the provider's assurance statement.
Covers accounts in the audited tenant only, judged against Auditex inactivity thresholds rather than your own policy. Accounts on devices and other services need other proof.
Default passwords on devices, software and services are not visible in tenant data.
Installed software and network services on devices are not visible in tenant data.
Auto-run settings on devices are not read by this audit.
Public sharing settings are clues only; they do not show how users authenticate to every service.
Device lock settings are not read by this audit.
Covers a few settings of the audited tenant only; every other cloud service needs its own proof.
Covers the operating system of managed devices only. Applications, firmware, servers and unmanaged devices need other proof.
Covers update ring assignment for managed Windows devices only; other software and devices need other proof.
Update policy and device state are clues, not proof of when a fix was installed; the assessor checks this by scanning sample devices.
For the cloud service the provider installs updates; the proof is your contract or the provider's assurance statement.
Account approval is a process record, not a tenant setting.
Whether each person has their own sign-in is not settled by tenant data.
Covers accounts in the audited tenant only, judged against Auditex inactivity thresholds; other systems need other proof.
Covers the audited tenant only. Policy, registration and enrolment are different facts, and per-user legacy MFA is not read. Every other cloud service needs its own proof.
Covers administrators of the audited tenant only; administrator accounts elsewhere need other proof.
Role and licence data are clues only; the assessor checks account separation on sample devices.
Covers privileged roles in the audited tenant only; rights on other systems need other proof.
Guessing limits on every service are not read by this audit.
Password rules on every service are not read by this audit.
Guidance given to users is a process record, not a tenant setting.
Supplier and service provider accounts need a list and process record beyond tenant data.
Covers Defender state on managed Windows devices only; the mail malware filter concerns mail flow and is no proof of endpoint protection.
Application allow-listing is not read by this audit.
For the cloud service the provider runs malware protection; the proof is your contract or the provider's assurance statement.

actions.title: Re-run the audit with the missing permission, licence or collector
actions.proof_to_gather: Grant the read permission or licence the unknown rules name, turn on the collector they need, then run the audit again and use the new bundle.

actions.title: Run the audit again to refresh old evidence
actions.proof_to_gather: Run a fresh audit so the evidence an assessor sees is recent; this bundle is older than the catalogue allows.

actions.title: Record the reason behind an accepted gap
actions.proof_to_gather: Write down who accepted the gap, why, until when and what reduces the risk meanwhile. An Auditex waiver is your own record, not a scheme exemption, so the gap still needs closing or the assessor's view.

actions.title: Keep the cloud provider's contract or assurance statement
actions.proof_to_gather: Keep the part of the provider's contract, terms or published assurance statement that commits them to run firewalls, security updates and malware protection for the service.

actions.title: Disable or remove the stale Microsoft 365 accounts
actions.proof_to_gather: Disable or delete each enabled account, guest or privileged account the audit found unused, or record why it is still needed, then re-run the audit.

actions.title: Block legacy authentication and tenant-wide SMTP AUTH
actions.proof_to_gather: Block legacy authentication with Conditional Access and turn off SMTP AUTH for the whole organisation, allowing it only on the mailboxes that need it.

actions.title: Restrict user consent to applications
actions.proof_to_gather: Limit user consent to verified publishers with low-risk permissions, or turn it off and use the admin consent workflow.

actions.title: Upgrade or retire devices on an unsupported operating system
actions.proof_to_gather: Upgrade each managed device whose operating system is out of support, or take it out of scope, and keep the list of what changed.

actions.title: Assign update rings and shorten long deferrals
actions.proof_to_gather: Assign a Windows update ring to every managed device group and keep quality update deferral short enough to install fixes within 14 days.

actions.title: Bring stale managed devices back into sync
actions.proof_to_gather: Find the managed devices that have not checked in recently, bring them back online or retire them, so their update state is current.

actions.title: Require MFA for every user and administrator in Conditional Access
actions.proof_to_gather: Change Conditional Access or security defaults so every user and every administrator role must use MFA, with exclusions limited to the named emergency access accounts, then re-run the audit.

actions.title: Register an MFA method for every listed account
actions.proof_to_gather: Have each user and administrator the audit lists register an MFA method, then re-run the audit to show the registration.

actions.title: Turn on Defender protection and update signatures
actions.proof_to_gather: Turn on antivirus and real-time protection and bring signatures up to date on each managed Windows device the audit lists.

actions.title: Restore the mail malware filter
actions.proof_to_gather: Restore the Exchange Online malware filter settings the audit flagged. This covers mail flow only and is no proof of endpoint protection.

actions.title: Suspend or remove the stale Google Workspace accounts
actions.proof_to_gather: Suspend or delete each user or administrator the audit found unused, including accounts with no recorded sign-in, or record why it is still needed, then re-run the audit.

actions.title: Replace ChromeOS devices past auto-update expiry
actions.proof_to_gather: Replace or retire each ChromeOS device past its auto-update expiry, and keep the list of what changed.

actions.title: Enforce 2-step verification for every user and administrator
actions.proof_to_gather: Turn on 2-step verification enforcement for every organisational unit and group that holds users or administrators.

actions.title: Enrol every listed account in 2-step verification
actions.proof_to_gather: Have each user and administrator the audit lists enrol in 2-step verification, then re-run the audit to show the enrolment.

actions.title: Explain why accounts under an MFA policy have no method registered
actions.proof_to_gather: The policy requires MFA yet some accounts have no method registered. Find out whether they are new, unused or excluded, then register or disable them.

actions.title: Explain why accounts under enforced 2-step verification are not enrolled
actions.proof_to_gather: Enforcement is on yet some accounts are not enrolled. Find out whether they are new, in a grace period or not signing in, then enrol or suspend them.

actions.title: Explain why devices with an update ring are out of date
actions.proof_to_gather: Update rings are assigned yet devices run an unsupported system or have not synced. Check each listed device, then update, reconnect or retire it.

actions.title: Show unused accounts are removed outside this tenant
actions.proof_to_gather: Keep a list of accounts on devices, other cloud services and network equipment, with the date each unused one was removed or disabled.

actions.title: Show every other cloud service is configured securely
actions.proof_to_gather: List the other cloud services in scope and keep a record of the settings that limit each to the services required.

actions.title: Keep an inventory of supported software
actions.proof_to_gather: Keep a software and device inventory that shows each item is licensed and supported, including devices no management tool sees.

actions.title: Show automatic updates are on beyond managed devices
actions.proof_to_gather: Record that automatic updates are turned on for software and devices the tenant does not manage, or how they are updated instead.

actions.title: Keep per-device evidence of fixes installed within 14 days
actions.proof_to_gather: Keep a patch report per device that shows when each high or critical fix was released and installed. Update policy alone does not show fix age.

actions.title: Keep the leaver and inactivity procedure
actions.proof_to_gather: Keep the procedure that disables accounts when people leave or after a set period of inactivity, with recent examples from other systems.

actions.title: List MFA for every other cloud service
actions.proof_to_gather: List every other cloud service in scope with how MFA is turned on for it, or the record that it offers no MFA option.

actions.title: List MFA on administrator accounts outside this tenant
actions.proof_to_gather: List administrator accounts on other services and devices reachable from the internet, with how MFA protects each.

actions.title: Keep the review of special access rights
actions.proof_to_gather: Keep the latest review of administrator and other special rights across systems, with the rights removed since.

actions.title: Show malware protection on every in-scope device
actions.proof_to_gather: List every in-scope device with its malware protection product, its status and its last update, including devices no management tool sees.

actions.title: Show a firewall protects every in-scope device
actions.proof_to_gather: Record the firewall on each device type and network boundary, with its settings, for devices and networks the tenant cannot see.

actions.title: Show firewall admin interfaces are protected
actions.proof_to_gather: Record that default firewall passwords were changed and that each admin interface is closed to the internet or protected by MFA or an address allow list.

actions.title: Keep the approved inbound firewall rules
actions.proof_to_gather: Export the inbound firewall rules with who approved each and why, and remove rules no longer needed.

actions.title: List the services reachable from the internet
actions.proof_to_gather: List public addresses and the services on each, with why each is needed, ready for the assessor's remote scan.

actions.title: Show default passwords were changed
actions.proof_to_gather: Record that default or guessable passwords were changed on devices, software and services when they were set up.

actions.title: Show unneeded software and services are removed
actions.proof_to_gather: Keep the device build standard or a recent review that shows unneeded software, utilities and network services were removed or turned off.

actions.title: Show auto-run is turned off
actions.proof_to_gather: Record the device setting that stops files running automatically without the user agreeing.

actions.title: Show users sign in before reaching data or services
actions.proof_to_gather: Record how users authenticate before reaching organisational data or services, including shared and public links.

actions.title: Show device unlock settings
actions.proof_to_gather: Record the device lock setting: a PIN or password of at least 6 characters, or biometrics, with protection against guessing.

actions.title: Keep the account approval process
actions.proof_to_gather: Keep the process for creating and approving user accounts, with recent approvals as examples.

actions.title: Show users have their own credentials
actions.proof_to_gather: Record that each person signs in with their own account and that shared accounts are not used.

actions.title: Show administrators use separate admin accounts
actions.proof_to_gather: List each administrator with their everyday account and separate admin account, ready for the assessor to check on sample devices.

actions.title: Show password guessing is limited
actions.proof_to_gather: Record how each service limits password guessing: MFA, throttling, or lock-out after no more than 10 guesses in 5 minutes.

actions.title: Show how password quality is enforced
actions.proof_to_gather: Record how password quality is enforced on each service: MFA, a 12-character minimum, or 8 characters with a deny list.

actions.title: Keep the password guidance given to users
actions.proof_to_gather: Keep the guidance users receive on choosing unique passwords and the process for changing a password that may be compromised.

actions.title: List supplier and service provider accounts
actions.proof_to_gather: List accounts used by suppliers and managed service providers, with how each is approved, protected by MFA and removed.

actions.title: Show only approved applications can run
actions.proof_to_gather: If you rely on allow-listing instead of anti-malware, record the list of approved, code-signed applications and how it is enforced.

actions.title: Prepare the address and service list for the remote scan
actions.proof_to_gather: Give the assessor the public addresses and services in scope, and keep a place for their scan results. Tenant data is not an exposure scan.

actions.title: Prepare the device sample and update evidence for the patch scan
actions.proof_to_gather: Give the assessor the device inventory to sample from and the update evidence you hold. The assessor runs the authenticated scan.

actions.title: Prepare the per-device malware protection view
actions.proof_to_gather: Give the assessor the managed-device protection evidence and a checklist for devices and products outside it.

actions.title: Prepare sample accounts for the witnessed MFA sign-in
actions.proof_to_gather: Give the assessor the MFA policy and enrolment evidence and a sample of user and administrator accounts to sign in with in front of them.

actions.title: Prepare the list of administrator accounts for the separation check
actions.proof_to_gather: Give the assessor the administrator role list and the matching everyday accounts. A productivity licence on an admin account is only a clue.

conflicts.note: The MFA policy shows no gap, yet users have no MFA method registered.
The administrator MFA policy shows no gap, yet administrators have no MFA method registered.
2-step verification enforcement shows no gap, yet users are not enrolled.
2-step verification enforcement for administrators shows no gap, yet administrators are not enrolled.
Update rings are assigned, yet devices run an unsupported system or have not synced recently.

assessor_tests.title: Remote exposure
assessor_tests.auditex_prepares: A customer-owned list of public addresses and services, and a place to attach the assessor's results. Tenant data is not an exposure scan.
assessor_tests.assessor_witnesses: The assessor finds the in-scope public addresses and checks which services can be reached from the internet.

assessor_tests.title: Vulnerability and patching
assessor_tests.framework_label: Test case 2: Check patching, by authenticated vulnerability scan of devices
assessor_tests.auditex_prepares: A device inventory to sample from and the device update evidence the tenant holds. It cannot reproduce the scan or tell fix age from an update policy.
assessor_tests.assessor_witnesses: The assessor runs an authenticated vulnerability scan of sample devices, including servers and IaaS hosts in scope, and checks that each fix for a vulnerability rated high or critical, scored CVSS 7 or above, or released without a published severity was applied within 14 days of release.

assessor_tests.title: Malware protection
assessor_tests.auditex_prepares: A per-device view of managed-device protection evidence and a checklist for products and devices outside it.
assessor_tests.assessor_witnesses: The assessor checks malware protection directly on sample devices.

assessor_tests.title: Multi-factor authentication
assessor_tests.framework_label: Test case 4: Check multi-factor authentication configuration
assessor_tests.auditex_prepares: Tenant policy and enrolment evidence, a sample of user and administrator accounts and a place to record the witnessed sign-in. Logs and settings do not replace the witnessed sign-in.
assessor_tests.assessor_witnesses: The assessor watches sample users and administrators sign in to each cloud service from a private or untrusted browser and sees MFA requested.

assessor_tests.title: Account separation
assessor_tests.auditex_prepares: Role and account clues and a request for the assessor's witnessed check. A productivity licence on an admin account is only a clue.
assessor_tests.assessor_witnesses: The assessor checks on sample devices and cloud services that administrators use separate accounts for admin work.
